summary.intent: Investigate feasibility of writable shares in CipherBox and create Phase 27 (Writable Shares PoC) — adding the phase to the roadmap, capturing implementation decisions, and beginning the planning pipeline.
summary.outcome: Phase 27 added to roadmap with CONTEXT.md and RESEARCH.md created. VALIDATION.md written. Planning pipeline blocked at UI design contract gate requiring /gsd:ui-phase 27 to complete before /gsd:plan-phase 27 can proceed.

repo: CipherBox's server-relayed IPNS architecture sidesteps the general 'unsolved multi-writer IPNS' problem — all publishes go through the API, which acts as the coordination point, making multi-writer conflict detection equivalent to existing multi-device sync.

Vault-level IPNS keys (vault, key blob, device registry, BYO-IPFS config) are HKDF-derived from the secp256k1 private key to enable self-sovereign discovery before any decryption. Folder and file IPNS keys are randomly generated because their IPNS name is discoverable from parent folder metadata.

File IPNS keys were deliberately migrated from HKDF-derived to random in a pre-Phase 14 todo specifically to enable future write-sharing — deterministic derivation would have required sharing the root secp256k1 private key to share IPNS publish authority.

Phase 14 (user-to-user sharing) is read-only only; writable sharing was explicitly deferred and is the design target for Phase 27. TEAM-11 in M4 requirements plans a full cryptographic read/write key hierarchy.

The conflict resolution infrastructure (expectedSequenceNumber check, 409 retry, withConflictRetry, 30s polling) already handles the multi-writer case correctly — Phase 27 adds no new conflict logic, just IPNS key delivery to recipients.

code.finding: Optimistic concurrency: expectedSequenceNumber checked server-side before every IPNS publish
409 conflict detection with automatic single-retry + re-sync after sequence mismatch
UI conflict banner with jitter-delayed retry
Sequence comparison across network vs DB cache — highest wins
Subfolder IPNS keys use generateEd25519Keypair() — random, not derived, enabling independent shareability
Vault-level IPNS keys derived via HKDF from secp256k1 key for recovery-phrase-based self-sovereign discovery
File IPNS keys use generateFileIpnsKeypair() — random, migrated away from HKDF derivation
Documents the rationale for switching file IPNS keys to random: deterministic design would have prevented write-sharing on individual files
Security review for the IPNS key randomization migration
